newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end at record, deregulation delayed.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end at record, deregulation delayed.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended at a record high for the third consecutive day on Friday despite a government announcement that an economic deregulation package had been postponed to next week, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index ended 1.11 points, or 0.15 percent, up at the day high of 736.60 points after touching a day low of 733.89 points.
Advancers led decliners by 66 to 60 with 68 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 547 billion rupiah.
The index closed at 716.83 points last week.
Brokers said the market had moved within a tight range most of the day as players were waiting for details of the long-awaited economic deregulation package.
State Secretary Murdiono however said the measures will be announced next week after some fine-tuning.
Sources in the finance ministry had earlier said the measures were likely to be announced during the day.

Digby Falkner, head of research for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Asia Indonesia, said the upcoming deregulation package would provide a better business environment and attract more investment in Indonesia.
